tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no skills — tests fixture-only.

OWNED FILES (only these; everything except triage_agent.py and its tests is new):
  factory/triage_agent.py
  tests/test_triage_agent.py
  deploy/triage-triggers/loop-factory-triage@.service
  deploy/triage-triggers/outbox-watch@.path
  deploy/triage-triggers/outbox-watch@.service
  deploy/triage-triggers/install_triggers.py
  tests/test_triage_triggers.py

CONTEXT — owner design (Ankit, 2026-08-02, verbatim intent): 'self heal should be a trigger not a timer — on failure, call it in to heal, and that's based on the goal of the loops and processes.' factory/triage_agent.py exists at HEAD (read it fully): cursor-based outbox consumer, deterministic classes, charter goal enrichment for objective breaches, propose-only Ringer manifests + selfheal cards, single cooldown-guarded digest. Your job: event-driven summons + arrival context.

BUILD:
1. factory/triage_agent.py gains two optional args, threaded into behavior and audit: --trigger-unit <systemd unit name> and --trigger-path <outbox path>. When present: (a) the run's audit rows and JSON receipt record trigger:{kind:'unit_failure'|'outbox_append'|'timer', ref}; (b) GOAL-FIRST PRIORITIZATION — resolve the trigger to a department (unit name prefix match against departments/* names and the registry files in estate/registry.d/*.yaml; outbox path parent department dir), load that department's charter, and put its items FIRST in classification/digest ordering, with the digest lead naming the summoning failure (e.g. '[triage] summoned by podcast-loop failure: ...'); (c) a unit-failure trigger for a unit that maps to NO department is still processed globally with trigger recorded and class infra_restartable candidate noted for that unit itself. Preserve every existing behavior and all 20 existing tests (extend, do not weaken; the cursor-EOF anti-bombardment property must remain).
2. deploy/triage-triggers/loop-factory-triage@.service — instance unit: Type=oneshot, ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m factory.triage_agent --repo-root {{REPO}} --config %h/.config/loop-factory/triage.yaml --execute --trigger-unit %i, WorkingDirectory={{REPO}}. House header comments (read templates/systemd/ files and match): installed via install_triggers.py, owner reviews.
3. deploy/triage-triggers/outbox-watch@.path + outbox-watch@.service — path unit watching a systemd-escaped path instance (PathModified=%f via the escaped instance — read systemd.path semantics carefully: use PathModified= with the unescaped path rendered by the installer instead if %f in .path is unreliable; the INSTALLER may render concrete per-outbox unit files rather than true template instances if that is more robust — your call, document it), triggering a triage run with --trigger-path.
4. deploy/triage-triggers/install_triggers.py — idempotent installer CLI (--repo-root, --user-unit-dir default ~/.config/systemd/user, --units <name>... for OnFailure hooks, --outboxes <path>..., --dry-run): (a) renders and writes the triage@ unit with {{REPO}} substituted; (b) writes per-outbox path/service unit pairs; (c) for each --units NAME, writes a drop-in ~/.config/systemd/user/NAME.service.d/10-triage-onfailure.conf containing [Unit] OnFailure=loop-factory-triage@%n.service — never modifying the unit file itself, only drop-ins; (d) prints a receipt JSON of files written and reminds daemon-reload; NEVER runs systemctl itself (the coordinator/owner does). Refuses to overwrite a non-matching existing drop-in without --force.
5. The hourly fallback stays: do not touch templates/systemd/loop-factory-triage.timer beyond (if trivial) a comment noting it is the deadman fallback behind event triggers.

tests/test_triage_triggers.py — at least 8 tests: --trigger-unit records trigger in receipt+audit; unit->department resolution via fixture registry/department layout puts that department's items first in the digest and the digest lead names the summoning unit; --trigger-path resolves the department from the path; unmappable unit still processed with trigger recorded; installer dry-run writes nothing and lists everything; installer writes drop-in with exact OnFailure line and is idempotent (second run no-op); installer refuses conflicting drop-in without --force; rendered triage@ unit contains the {{REPO}}-substituted paths. Extend tests/test_triage_agent.py only if an existing test needs the new args threaded (do not delete tests).

VERIFY: 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 loopfactory.py check' full suite green. You fail for touching files outside the owned list, fewer than 8 new 'def test_' functions in test_triage_triggers.py, or the verify command failing.
tasks.verified: failures now summon the healer: OnFailure drop-ins and outbox path-watchers call the triage agent with arrival context, and it prioritizes the summoning department's goals — timer demoted to deadman fallback
